title: The Autopsy of Little Hawley
premise: Cyrus Okafor, the night concierge of the Hotel Verity in Little Hawley, has spent a decade watching guests arrive and disappear without ever asking questions. When twin letters arrive at her desk — one confessing to the unsolved drowning of a child twelve years ago, one promising a second death before the trial begins — she realizes both were written in her own handwriting. As Cyrus investigates her stolen identity, she uncovers a conspiracy among the town's founding families to bury what really happened at the old Hawley estate, and discovers the killer is someone who has been watching her as long as she has watched others. In the end, Cyrus must choose between protecting the only person who ever made her feel she belonged and delivering the truth that will finally close the case — and she does, testifying at trial after letting the killer walk free just long enough to be caught in the act.
about_author: Jonah Sandoval is the pen name of a former hotel night auditor who spent eleven years working the graveyard shift in small coastal towns, collecting the stories guests tell when they think no one is listening. The Autopsy of Little Hawley is their second novel and first mystery.

chapters.title: The Night Desk
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus Okafor. A quiet shift at the Hotel Verity establishes Cyrus's gift for noticing everything — the guest who lies about his wife, the maid who cries in stairwell three. She prides herself on observing without involvement. Emotional beat: comfortable detachment, about to be shattered.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Two letters arrive addressed to her: one confesses to the drowning of eight-year-old Etta Hawley twelve years ago; the other promises 'the second one' will die before trial. Both are written in Cyrus's handwriting. Emotional beat: vertigo — her private self turned into evidence.

chapters.title: What the Register Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. She pulls the hotel's archived registers from the summer Etta died and finds her own signature on dates she was never in town. Someone has been building a false Cyrus for years. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Quit
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Cyrus and ex-detective Marisol Vane. Cyrus tracks down the investigator who walked away from the Hawley case; Marisol warns her the file was sanitized from above. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Trial in Sixty Days
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. The county announces the trial of Denny Foss, the handyman long suspected in Etta's death. Marisol realizes the confession letter could destroy or save him — depending whose hands it lands in. Emotional beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. She maps Little Hawley's power structure — the Hawleys, the Brandts, Judge Ellery Crane — and notices all three families checked into the Verity the week Etta died. Emotional beat: the town itself becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: A Hand I Know
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Graphologist confirms the letters are genuine imitations, learned over time — meaning someone with long access to Cyrus's writing. She inventory-checks every note, card, and ledger she's ever signed. Emotional beat: paranoia blooms.

chapters.title: The Second One
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. A witness from the original case, Ruthie Brandt, survives a staged overdose hours after telling Cyrus she remembered 'the well house.' The second death was attempted, not promised. Emotional beat: the threat turns real and urgent.

chapters.title: Etta's Summer
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. Flashback chapter reconstructing the original investigation through Marisol's memory — the pressure to close fast, the evidence that pointed toward the estate and away from Denny Foss. Emotional beat: guilt as fuel.

chapters.title: The Well House
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus breaks into the derelict Hawley estate and finds the well house sealed with new hardware — someone still maintains it. Inside, a child's shoe and a ledger of payments. Emotional beat: grief surfacing under adrenaline.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Interlude: Cyrus remembers Theo, the mentor who hired her a decade ago and gave her a home when she had none — and realizes his handwriting lessons explain her forged hand. Emotional beat: loyalty and suspicion tearing at each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The ledger records monthly payments to 'D.F.' for silence — Denny Foss took money to confess to a crime he didn't commit. Marisol confronts him; he recants, terrified. Emotional beat: the case inverts entirely.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching Me Watch
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus discovers her own movements documented in meticulous notes hidden in the hotel's lost-and-found — her life catalogued for years by someone who learned observation from her. Emotional beat: hunter realizing she is also prey.

chapters.title: Judge Crane's Favor
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. Marisol digs into Judge Ellery Crane and finds he signed the order sealing the Hawley autopsy — which listed injuries inconsistent with drowning. Emotional beat: the conspiracy reaches the courtroom itself.

chapters.title: The Confession I Never Wrote
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus stages a trap: she plants a false detail about the well house in a note only staff would see. Within a day, the well house is cleaned out. Her forger works inside the hotel. Emotional beat: cold clarity — turning her gift into a weapon.

chapters.title: Narrowing
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Three suspects remain: Theo, the head housekeeper Agnes, and night porter Cole. Each had access, motive threads, and handwriting exposure. Marisol warns Cyrus the trial date moved up. Emotional beat: compression, rising panic.

chapters.title: What Theo Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Searching Theo's office, Cyrus finds Etta's missing second shoe and photographs proving Theo witnessed the real death — but not who caused it. He was paid to stay silent too. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the father figure complicit.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Promise
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Cyrus decodes the second letter's phrasing and realizes 'the second one' means the second witness to the truth: her. The killer didn't frame her randomly — she was always meant to take the fall. Emotional beat: terror fused with resolve.

chapters.title: Night of the Verdict Eve
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. On the eve of trial, Cyrus baits the killer with a fake confession naming them, left where only they would find it. The hotel goes dark — power cut. Footsteps on the service stairs. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Agnes
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The killer is Agnes, Etta's aunt, who covered up an accidental death that the family would have blamed on her — then killed to keep it buried, forging Cyrus because Cyrus once saw her burning papers years ago. Confrontation in the flooded basement. Emotional beat: climax — violence, confession, near-drowning mirrored against Etta's.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. Trial begins; Denny Foss is freed, Agnes arrested, Judge Crane recused under scandal. Cyrus testifies, choosing truth over the town's comfort and over Theo's freedom from shame. Emotional beat: costly vindication.

chapters.title: Morning Shift
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Weeks later, Cyrus returns to the night desk, changed — she now speaks to guests instead of merely watching them. A new arrival checks in carrying an envelope, and Cyrus, unafraid, opens it herself. Emotional beat: belonging found in engagement, not distance; quiet promise of more.
